linkedin.text:
On July 2, 2026, Microsoft launched Frontier, a business backed by $2.5 billion and roughly 6,000 engineers, as The Next Web reported.

Their job is to sit inside customers' companies and make the AI those customers already paid for work. The companies that sell AI models paid to put people next to the customer because selling the model alone didn't move the numbers.

If your own pilot gave you a good demo and nothing on the bottom line, you're in the majority. MIT's NANDA researchers found that 95% of enterprise generative-AI pilots produce no measurable profit-and-loss impact, across more than 300 deployments.

Rob Richardson's post names four places a pilot usually dies: name the job, fit the workflow, own the handoff, prove the number. A person decides all four. We'd check them before you blame the tool.

Outside engineers are fine as a jumpstart. If your own people never learn those four steps, you've bought a dependency that walks out the door when the contract ends. Teach them, and the skill stays with you after that.

Which of the four is your pilot missing?

Read the full post: https://disruptionnow.com/blog/you-don-t-have-a-model-problem
